title: A Paint-On Liquid Can Stop Cavities
summary:
A cavity does not have to mean drilling. A simple liquid painted on a tooth in seconds can stop tooth decay in young children. A big test has now shown that it works.

The liquid is called silver diamine fluoride, or SDF. A dentist paints it on the cavity with a tiny sponge-tipped stick. There is no drilling, no shot, and no sleep medicine.

SDF stops the decay from getting worse. It does not put back tooth parts that are already gone. Its silver fights the germs linked to decay, and its fluoride helps make the tooth stronger.

The test, shared in JAMA Pediatrics, included 830 children younger than 6 from Michigan, New York, and Iowa. Margherita Fontana, a dentistry professor at the University of Michigan and the study's lead researcher, said the treatment is very effective and safe, even for children as young as 1.

There is one downside. SDF turns the decayed part of the tooth dark for good. The change is mostly about looks. For many families, skipping pain and drilling matters more.
why_it_matters: If you ever get a cavity, this liquid could let a dentist stop it without drilling or pain.

background_read: Tooth decay is damage to a tooth caused by germs that live in the mouth.
Fluoride is a mineral that helps make tooth enamel stronger and protects teeth from decay.
Dentists usually treat cavities by removing the damaged part and filling the tooth, but a paint-on liquid can stop the decay without drilling.

WHY: To stop decay without drilling, shots, or sleep medicine.
